(Approval status: Phase I)

drugs.name: Pamiparib
drugs.description: Pamiparib (BGB-290) inhibits PARP1 and PARP2, potentially resulting in increased sensitivity to DNA damaging agents (AACR; 2015. Abstract nr 1651, PMID: 32652442).

associations.description: In a Phase I trial, CX-5461 treatment resulted in partial response in a patient with advanced solid tumor harboring BRCA2 mutations, and stable disease in 5 additional patients, 4 of whom harboring BRCA1/2 mutations, and 1 with Li-Fraumeni syndrome (Annals of Oncology, Volume 29, Issue suppl_3, 1 March 2018, abstract 440; NCT02719977). (Approval status: Phase I)

drugs.name: CX-5461
drugs.description: CX-5461 is an RNA polymerase I (Pol I) inhibitor that inhibits rRNA synthesis, resulting in growth arrest and apoptosis in cancer cells (PMID: 26472108, PMID: 32719798).

associations.description: Germline BRCA1/2 mutations are associated with increased risk of developing and early onset of pancreatic cancer (NCCN.org). (Approval status: Guideline)

references.title: NCCN.org

associations.description: In a retrospective study of a Phase III trial, ovarian carcinoma patients harboring a mutation in either BRCA1, BRCA2, or another homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene did not demonstrate a significant difference in progression free survival when Avastin (bevacizumab) was added to the combined platinum therapy, Platinol (carboplatin) and Taxol (paclitaxel), versus the platinum therapy with placebo, suggesting HRR gene mutations do not impact the effect of Avastin (bevacizumab) (PMID: 29191972). (Approval status: Clinical Study)

drugs.name: Bevacizumab
drugs.description: Avastin (bevacizumab) is a monoclonal antibody that binds VEGF and inhibits binding to VEGFR, potentially resulting in decreased tumor growth (PMID: 15136787). Avastin (bevacizumab) is FDA approved for use in colorectal cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, glioblastoma, renal cell carcinoma, cervical carcinoma, and ovarian cancer, and in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel in epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer (FDA.gov).

drugs.name: Carboplatin
drugs.description: Paraplatin (carboplatin) is a second-generation platinum compound and is activated intracellularly to form reactive platinum complexes that cross link DNA with DNA and with proteins. This induces apoptosis and inhibits cell growth (NCI Drug Dictionary).

drugs.name: Paclitaxel
drugs.description: Taxol (paclitaxel) binds to tubulin to inhibit microtubule disassembly, which results in decreased cell division, and also binds to the anti-apoptotic factor Bcl-2, promoting apoptosis (NCI Drug Dictionary).

associations.description: FOLFIRINOX is included in guidelines as a preferred neoadjuvant therapy for pancreatic adenocarcinoma patients harboring BRCA2 mutations with resectable/borderline resectable disease and as a preferred first-line therapy for patients with locally advanced or metastatic disease with good performance status (ECOG 0 -1) (NCCN.org). drugs.name: Oxaliplatin
drugs.description: Eloxatin (oxaliplatin) is comprised of a platinum complex, which causes DNA-platinum cross-links, inhibition of DNA replication and transcription, and cell toxicity, and is FDA approved for colorectal cancer (FDA.gov).

drugs.name: Fluorouracil
drugs.description: Adrucil (fluorouracil) is an antimetabolite chemotherapeutic agent, which interferes with DNA and RNA synthesis thereby preventing cancer cell growth and is FDA approved for colorectal, breast, stomach, and pancreatic cancer (FDA.gov).

drugs.name: Leucovorin
drugs.description: Wellcovorin (leucovorin) is a metabolite of folate that enhances the efficacy of fluoruracil (PMID: 32490554).

drugs.name: Irinotecan

associations.description: In a Phase I/II trial (TALAVE), induction therapy with Talzenna (talazoparib) followed by treatment with the combination of Bavencio (avelumab) and Talzenna (talazoparib) resulted in a response rate of 83% (10/12, all partial responses) and median progression-free survival of 9.3 months in patients with ERBB2 (HER2)-negative advanced breast cancer harboring mutations in BRCA1 or BRCA2 (Cancer Res (2023) 83 (8_Supplement): CT142; NCT03964532). (Approval status: Phase Ib/II)

drugs.name: Talazoparib
drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). Talzenna (talazoparib) is FDA approved for use in patients with ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, and in combination with Xtandi (enzalutamide) in patients with homologous recombination repair gene (ATM, ATR, BRCA1/2, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, MLH1, MRE11A, NBN, PALB2, or RAD51C)-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (FDA.gov).

drugs.name: Avelumab
drugs.description: Bavencio (avelumab) is a monoclonal antibody binds to human immunosuppressive ligand programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1, CD274) and blocks protein signaling, resulting in immune regulation and antitumor immunity (PMID: 26014098). Bavencio (avelumab) is FDA-approved for use in adult and pediatric patients of 12 years or older with metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma, as maintenance therapy in locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (UC), in locally advanced or metastatic UC that progressed following chemotherapy, and in combination with axitinib as first-line therapy in advanced renal cell carcinoma (FDA.gov).

associations.description: In a preclinical study, TNG348 inhibited viability of breast cancer cell lines harboring mutations in BRCA1 or BRCA2 in culture, and inhibited tumor growth in a cell line xenograft model (Cancer Res (2023) 83 (7_Supplement): 4968). (Approval status: Preclinical - Cell line xenograft)

(Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Cyclophosphamide
drugs.description: Cytoxan (cyclophosphamide) is an alkylating agent, which inhibits DNA replication (NCI Drug Dictionary). Cytoxan (cyclophosphamide) is FDA approved in multiple hematological malignancies, breast cancer, neuroblastoma, ovarian cancer, and retinoblastoma (NCI Drug Dictionary).

drugs.name: Veliparib
drugs.description: Veliparib (ABT-888) is a PARP1 and PARP2 inhibitor, which inhibits DNA repair and induces lethality in homologous recombination deficient cells, and may enhance the sensitivity of chemotherapeutic agents (PMID: 26251615, PMID: 31074636, PMID: 32452601).

drugs.name: Carboplatin
drugs.description: Paraplatin (carboplatin) is a second-generation platinum compound and is activated intracellularly to form reactive platinum complexes that cross link DNA with DNA and with proteins. This induces apoptosis and inhibits cell growth (NCI Drug Dictionary).

drugs.name: Paclitaxel
drugs.description: Taxol (paclitaxel) binds to tubulin to inhibit microtubule disassembly, which results in decreased cell division, and also binds to the anti-apoptotic factor Bcl-2, promoting apoptosis (NCI Drug Dictionary).

drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). associations.description: In a Phase II trial (TRITON2) that supported FDA approval, Rubraca (rucaparib) treatment resulted in an objective response rate of 43.5% (27/62) and a PSA response rate of 54.8% (63/115) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who progressed on 1 or more anti-androgen and 1 taxane-based therapy and harboring deleterious BRCA1/2 germline or somatic mutations as detected by approved assays, including nonsense, frameshift, rearrangement, splice site variants (PMID: 32795228; NCT02952534). (Approval status: FDA approved - On Companion Diagnostic)

drugs.name: Rucaparib
drugs.description: Rubraca (rucaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in accumulation of DNA damage and chemosensitization of tumor cells (PMID: 17363489). Rubraca (rucaparib) is FDA approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation, and for treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation (germline and/or somatic) who received anti-androgen therapy and a taxane-based therapy (FDA.gov).

(Approval status: FDA approved - On Companion Diagnostic)

associations.description: In a Phase I/II trial, Veliparib (ABT-888) in combination with Adrucil (fluorouracil) and Eloxatin (oxaliplatin) resulted in an objective response rate of 44% (8/18) in patients with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma harboring deleterious mutations in the homologous recombination, DNA damage response and repair genes, responses were achieved in patients harboring mutations in BRCA1(n=1), BRCA2 (n=6), and PALB2 (n=1) (PMID: 32669374; NCT01489865). (Approval status: Case Reports/Case Series)

drugs.name: Oxaliplatin
drugs.description: Eloxatin (oxaliplatin) is comprised of a platinum complex, which causes DNA-platinum cross-links, inhibition of DNA replication and transcription, and cell toxicity, and is FDA approved for colorectal cancer (FDA.gov).

drugs.name: Fluorouracil
drugs.description: Adrucil (fluorouracil) is an antimetabolite chemotherapeutic agent, which interferes with DNA and RNA synthesis thereby preventing cancer cell growth and is FDA approved for colorectal, breast, stomach, and pancreatic cancer (FDA.gov).

drugs.name: Veliparib
drugs.description: Veliparib (ABT-888) is a PARP1 and PARP2 inhibitor, which inhibits DNA repair and induces lethality in homologous recombination deficient cells, and may enhance the sensitivity of chemotherapeutic agents (PMID: 26251615, PMID: 31074636, PMID: 32452601).

associations.description: In a Phase III trial (BROCADE3), addition of Veliparib (ABT-888) to Paraplatin (carboplatin) and Taxol (paclitaxel) combination therapy significantly improved progression-free survival (14.5 vs 12.6 mo., HR=0.71, p=0.0016) compared to placebo in patients with Erbb2 (Her2)-negative breast cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA1/2 mutations (PMID: 32861273; NCT02163694). (Approval status: Phase III)

drugs.name: Carboplatin
drugs.description: Paraplatin (carboplatin) is a second-generation platinum compound and is activated intracellularly to form reactive platinum complexes that cross link DNA with DNA and with proteins. This induces apoptosis and inhibits cell growth (NCI Drug Dictionary).

drugs.name: Paclitaxel
drugs.description: Taxol (paclitaxel) binds to tubulin to inhibit microtubule disassembly, which results in decreased cell division, and also binds to the anti-apoptotic factor Bcl-2, promoting apoptosis (NCI Drug Dictionary).

associations.description: In a Phase I trial, Fluzoparib treatment was well tolerated and resulted in a median progression-free survival (mPFS) of 7.2 months among 43 ovarian cancer patients treated with >120mg/d, and a mPFS of 8.9 months among 11 evaluable patients with germline BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 mutations (7 BRCA1, 2 BRCA2, 2 BRCA1/BRCA2) treated with 80mg bid (n=1), 100mg bid (n=5), or 150mg bid (n=5) (PMID: 32694901; NCT03509636). (Approval status: Case Reports/Case Series)

drugs.name: Fluzoparib
drugs.description: Fluzoparib (SHR3162) is a PARP inhibitor, which potentially induces DNA damage, cell cycle arrest and apoptosis, and inhibits cell proliferation and tumor growth (PMID: 30663191, PMID: 32694901).

references.title: Phase I dose-escalation and expansion study of PARP inhibitor, fluzoparib (SHR3162), in patients with advanced solid tumors.

associations.description: In a Phase II trial (TBCRC 048), Lynparza (olaparib) treatment resulted in an objective response rate (ORR) of 31% (8/26) and a clinical benefit rate (CBR) at 18 weeks of 48% in patients with metastatic breast cancer harboring somatic mutations in homologous recombination-related genes, all responders harbored pathogenic mutations in BRCA1 (n=6) or BRCA2 (n=10), ORR and CBR in BRCA1/2-mutant patients were 50% and 66%, respectively (PMID: 33119476; NCT03344965). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Olaparib
drugs.description: Lynparza (olaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, resulting in inhibition of DNA repair and lethality in homologous-recombination deficient cells, and may be a sensitizing agent for chemotherapy and radiotherapy (PMID: 25028150, PMID: 24225019). Lynparza (olaparib) is FDA approved for treatment of ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, ovarian cancer with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations and received 3 or more prior therapies, metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations as a maintenance therapy, metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline or somatic homologous recombination repair gene mutations who progressed following enzalutamide or abiraterone, in combination with abiraterone in patients with mCRPC harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA mutations, as a maintenance therapy in recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer and in epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline or somatic BRCA mutation, and in combination with Avastin (bevacizumab) as maintenance therapy in HDR defective epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer as defined by deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA mutation, and/or genomic instability (FDA.gov).

references.title: TBCRC 048: Phase II Study of Olaparib for Metastatic Breast Cancer and Mutations in Homologous Recombination-Related Genes.

(Approval status: Guideline)

drugs.name: Talazoparib
drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). Talzenna (talazoparib) is FDA approved for use in patients with ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, and in combination with Xtandi (enzalutamide) in patients with homologous recombination repair gene (ATM, ATR, BRCA1/2, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, MLH1, MRE11A, NBN, PALB2, or RAD51C)-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (FDA.gov).

(Approval status: Phase II)

associations.description: In a Phase II trial (Lung-MAP Sub-Study, S1900A), Rubraca (rucaparib) treatment in advanced non-small cell lung cancer patients harboring inactivating mutations in BRCA1 or BRCA2 and/or genomic loss of heterozygosity (>=21%) resulted in an objective response rate of 7% (4/59), which failed to meet the required level of efficacy for continuation of the S1900A clinical sub-study for both the squamous and non-squamous NSCLC cohorts (J Clin Oncol 39, no. 15_suppl (May 20, 2021) 9024; NCT03845296). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Rucaparib
drugs.description: Rubraca (rucaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in accumulation of DNA damage and chemosensitization of tumor cells (PMID: 17363489). Rubraca (rucaparib) is FDA approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation, and for treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation (germline and/or somatic) who received anti-androgen therapy and a taxane-based therapy (FDA.gov).

associations.description: In a Phase I trial, JPI-547 treatment in advanced solid tumor patients with BRCA1/2 or HRR mutations led to an objective response rate of 28.2% (11/39, all partial responses (PR)), with an ongoing PR in a BRCA2-mutant breast cancer (BC) patient, a disease control rate of 64.1% (25/39), stable disease (SD) in 15 patients, with ongoing SD in a BRCA-mutant BC patient, 3.5 mo median progression-free survival, and 3.4 mo median duration of treatment of (J Clin Oncol 39, 2021 (suppl 15; abstr 3113); NCT04335604). (Approval status: Phase I)

drugs.name: JPI-547
drugs.description: JPI-547 inhibits PARP1/2 and Tankyrase 1/2, potentially leading to anti-tumor activity (J Clin Oncol 39, no. 15_suppl (May 20, 2021) 3113).

associations.description: In a Phase II trial, maintenance Rubraca (rucaparib) resulted in a median progression-free survival (mPFS) of 13.1 months and an objective response rate (ORR) of 41.7% (15/36, 3 complete responses, 12 partial responses) in patients with platinum-sensitive, advanced pancreatic cancer harboring deleterious mutations in BRCA1/2 or PALB2, ORR was 40.7% (11/27) in patients with germline BRCA2 mutations and 50% (1/2) in patients with somatic BRCA2 mutations (PMID: 33970687; NCT03140670). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Rucaparib
drugs.description: Rubraca (rucaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in accumulation of DNA damage and chemosensitization of tumor cells (PMID: 17363489). Rubraca (rucaparib) is FDA approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation, and for treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation (germline and/or somatic) who received anti-androgen therapy and a taxane-based therapy (FDA.gov).

references.title: Phase II Study of Maintenance Rucaparib in Patients With Platinum-Sensitive Advanced Pancreatic Cancer and a Pathogenic Germline or Somatic Variant in BRCA1, BRCA2, or PALB2.

(Approval status: Case Reports/Case Series)

associations.description: In a Phase II trial, patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma harboring either a germline BRCA1, BRCA2, or PALB2 inactivating mutation demonstrated a response rate of 65.2% (15/23), a median progression-free survival of 9.7 months, a median overall survival of 16.4 months, and a disease control rate of 78.3% (18/23) when treated with a combination of Gemzar (gemcitabine) and Platinol (cisplatin) (PMID: 31976786). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Gemcitabine
drugs.description: Gemzar (gemcitabine) is converted in cells to difluorodeoxycytidine di- and triphosphate (dFdCDP, dFdCTP), which act to inhibit ribonucleoside reductase and as a deoxynucleotide analog respectively, resulting in DNA strand termination and apoptosis (NCI Drug Dictionary).

drugs.name: Cisplatin
drugs.description: Platinol (cisplatin) is a platinum based chemotherapeutic, which is FDA approved for bladder, ovarian, and testicular cancers (NCI Drug Dictionary).

associations.description: In a Phase I trial, neoadjuvant Zejula (niraparib) treatment with or without subsequent chemotherapy resulted in a tumor response (>/= 30% volume reduction by MRI after two treatment cycles) rate of 90.5% (19/21; 2 complete, 17 partial responses) in patients with Erbb2 (Her2)-negative localized breast cancer harboring inactivating BRCA1/2 mutations, with a pathological complete response (pCR) in 40% (6/15) of patients who received only Zejula (niraparib) prior to surgery (PMID: 35788722; NCT03329937). (Approval status: Phase I)

drugs.name: Niraparib
drugs.description: Zejula (niraparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in the accumulation of DNA damage and apoptosis of tumor cells (PMID: 23810788). Zejula (niraparib) is FDA-approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer in complete or partial response to first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, and as maintenance therapy in patients with advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations and in complete or partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy (FDA.gov).

references.title: Neoadjuvant study of niraparib in patients with HER2-negative, BRCA-mutated, resectable breast cancer.

drugs.name: KSQ-4279

associations.description: In a Phase II trial (TAPUR), Lynparza (olaparib) treatment in patients with advanced solid tumors harboring a mutation in BRCA1 or BRCA2 led to an objective response rate of 25% (8/32, 2 complete responses (CR) and 6 partial responses (PR), with 1 CR and 4 PRs in patients with BRCA2 mutations), a disease control rate of 41% (13/32), a median progression-free survival of 15.7 weeks, and an overall survival of 45 weeks (Ann Oncol (2022) 33 (suppl_7): S583-S584; NCT02693535). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Olaparib
drugs.description: Lynparza (olaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, resulting in inhibition of DNA repair and lethality in homologous-recombination deficient cells, and may be a sensitizing agent for chemotherapy and radiotherapy (PMID: 25028150, PMID: 24225019). Lynparza (olaparib) is FDA approved for treatment of ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, ovarian cancer with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations and received 3 or more prior therapies, metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations as a maintenance therapy, metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline or somatic homologous recombination repair gene mutations who progressed following enzalutamide or abiraterone, in combination with abiraterone in patients with mCRPC harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA mutations, as a maintenance therapy in recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer and in epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline or somatic BRCA mutation, and in combination with Avastin (bevacizumab) as maintenance therapy in HDR defective epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer as defined by deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA mutation, and/or genomic instability (FDA.gov).

associations.description: In a Phase III trial (ARIEL4), Rubraca (rucaparib) treatment resulted in an improved median progression-free survival (7.4 months vs 5.7 months, p=0.0010) and similar objective response rate (40% vs 32%) compared to standard-of-care chemotherapy in patients with relapsed ovarian, fallopian tube, or peritoneal cancer harboring deleterious germline or somatic BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations (PMID: 35298906; NCT02855944). (Approval status: Phase III)

drugs.name: Rucaparib
drugs.description: Rubraca (rucaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in accumulation of DNA damage and chemosensitization of tumor cells (PMID: 17363489). Rubraca (rucaparib) is FDA approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation, and for treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation (germline and/or somatic) who received anti-androgen therapy and a taxane-based therapy (FDA.gov).

references.title: Rucaparib versus standard-of-care chemotherapy in patients with relapsed ovarian cancer and a deleterious BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation (ARIEL4): an international, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial.

associations.description: In a Phase II trial (BAYOU), Lynparza (olaparib) and Imfinzi (durvalumab) improved median progression-free survival (5.6 vs 1.8 mo, HR 0.18) compared to Imfinzi (durvalumab) and placebo in a subgroup of patients with metastatic urothelial carcinoma harboring inactivating mutations in DNA damage repair genes (n=17), with 4.6% of the tumors harboring BRCA2 inactivating mutations (PMID: 35737919; NCT03459846). (Approval status: Case Reports/Case Series)

drugs.name: Durvalumab
drugs.description: Imfinzi (durvalumab) is a monoclonal antibody that binds to and inhibits PD-L1 (CD274), potentially resulting in increased immune response to tumors (PMID: 25943534, PMID: 28214651). associations.description: In a Phase II trial (JAVELIN), Talzenna (talazoparib) plus Bavencio (avelumab) did not meet prespecified futility requirements with an objective response rate (ORR) of 26.4% (42/159, 9 complete and 33 partial responses) in advanced solid tumor patients harboring BRCA1/2 inactivating mutations, and ORR was 32.0% (39/122) in BRCA-dependent (breast, ovarian, prostate, pancreatic cancer, uterine leiomyosarcoma) and 8.1% (3/37) in non-BRCA-dependent tumor types (PMID: 36394867; NCT03565991). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Talazoparib
drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). Talzenna (talazoparib) is FDA approved for use in patients with ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, and in combination with Xtandi (enzalutamide) in patients with homologous recombination repair gene (ATM, ATR, BRCA1/2, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, MLH1, MRE11A, NBN, PALB2, or RAD51C)-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (FDA.gov).

drugs.name: Avelumab
drugs.description: Bavencio (avelumab) is a monoclonal antibody binds to human immunosuppressive ligand programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1, CD274) and blocks protein signaling, resulting in immune regulation and antitumor immunity (PMID: 26014098). Bavencio (avelumab) is FDA-approved for use in adult and pediatric patients of 12 years or older with metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma, as maintenance therapy in locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (UC), in locally advanced or metastatic UC that progressed following chemotherapy, and in combination with axitinib as first-line therapy in advanced renal cell carcinoma (FDA.gov).

associations.description: In a Phase III trial (TRITON3), Rubraca (rucaparib) treatment resulted in improved imaging-based progression-free survival (11.2 months vs. 6.4 months, HR=0.5, p<0.001) compared to control treatment with Taxotere (docetaxel) in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring deleterious BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations, with a median overall survival of 24.3 months vs. 20.8 months, and confirmed objective response in 45% (37/82) vs. 17% (7/41) of patients (PMID: 36795891; NCT02975934). (Approval status: Phase III)

drugs.name: Rucaparib
drugs.description: Rubraca (rucaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in accumulation of DNA damage and chemosensitization of tumor cells (PMID: 17363489). Rubraca (rucaparib) is FDA approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation, and for treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation (germline and/or somatic) who received anti-androgen therapy and a taxane-based therapy (FDA.gov).

associations.description: In a clinical study, cholangiocarcinoma patients with a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation treated with a platinum-based therapy (n=13) or PARP inhibitor (n=4) demonstrated a median overall survival of 40.27 months for patients with stage I/II disease, and 25 months for patients with stage III/IV disease, with one patient harboring a BRCA2 mutation who received a PARP inhibitor experiencing a progression-free survival of 42.6 months and overall survival of 64.76 months (PMID: 28487467). (Approval status: Clinical Study - Cohort)

associations.description: In a Phase III trial (PROpel) that supported FDA approval, Zytiga (abiraterone) plus Lynparza (olaparib) improved median overall survival (42.1 vs 34.7 mo, HR 0.81, p=0.054) compared to Zytiga (abiraterone) and placebo in castration-resistant prostate cancer patients, with greater benefit in those harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA mutations (HR 0.29) as detected by approved assays, including nonsense, frameshift, rearrangement, and splice site variants (PMID: 37714168; NCT03732820). associations.description: In a Phase I trial, Talzenna (talazoparib) treatment resulted in an objective response rate of 50% (7/14, 1 complete response, 6 partial responses), a clinical benefit rate of 85.7%, and a median progression-free survival of 34.6 weeks in breast cancer patients harboring germline deleterious BRCA1/2 mutations (PMID: 28242752; NCT01286987). (Approval status: Phase I)

drugs.name: Talazoparib
drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). Talzenna (talazoparib) is FDA approved for use in patients with ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, and in combination with Xtandi (enzalutamide) in patients with homologous recombination repair gene (ATM, ATR, BRCA1/2, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, MLH1, MRE11A, NBN, PALB2, or RAD51C)-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (FDA.gov).

references.title: Phase I, Dose-Escalation, Two-Part Trial of the PARP Inhibitor Talazoparib in Patients with Advanced Germline BRCA1/2 Mutations and Selected Sporadic Cancers.

associations.description: In a Phase I trial, Talzenna (talazoparib) treatment resulted in a clinical benefit rate (CBR) of 56% (5/9) and a median progression-free survival (mPFS) of 20.4 weeks in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients harboring germline deleterious BRCA1/2 mutations, compared to a CBR of 89% (8/9) and a mPFS of 38.3 weeks in patients with non-TNBC (PMID: 28242752; NCT01286987). (Approval status: Case Reports/Case Series)

drugs.name: Atezolizumab
drugs.description: Tecentriq (atezolizumab) is a monoclonal antibody against PD-L1 (CD274), preventing activation of its receptor, potentially enhancing T-cell-mediated immune response to neoplasms and inhibiting T-cell inactivation (PMID: 29449897). Tecentriq (atezolizumab) is FDA approved for use in PD-L1 positive (IC >/= 5%) advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma not eligible for cisplatin-containing chemotherapy, in advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma not eligible for chemotherapy, in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) progressed on platinum-containing therapy, as first-line therapy in metastatic NSCLC with high PD-L1 expression (TC>/=50% or IC>/=10%) and without EGFR or ALK alterations, for adjuvant treatment in patients with PD-L1-positive (>=1% tumor cell expression) NSCLC, in combination with bevacizumab, paclitaxel, and carboplatin as first-line therapy for non-squamous NSCLC with no EGFR or ALK aberrations, in combination with paclitaxel protein-bound and carboplatin in metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with no EGFR or ALK aberrations, in combination with carboplatin and etoposide in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer, in combination with bevacizumab in hepatocellular carcinoma without prior systemic therapy, in combination with Cotellic (cobimetinib) and Zelboraf (vemurafenib) in unresectable or metastatic BRAF V600-mutated melanoma, and in pediatric and adult patients with unresectable or metastatic alveolar soft part sarcoma (FDA.gov).

drugs.name: Talazoparib
drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). Talzenna (talazoparib) is FDA approved for use in patients with ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, and in combination with Xtandi (enzalutamide) in patients with homologous recombination repair gene (ATM, ATR, BRCA1/2, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, MLH1, MRE11A, NBN, PALB2, or RAD51C)-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (FDA.gov).

drugs.name: Enzalutamide
drugs.description: Xtandi (enzalutamide) is a second-generation small molecule inhibitor of androgen receptor, thereby resulting in decreased tumor growth (PMID: 24009414, PMID: 25945058). Xtandi (enzalutamide) is FDA-approved for use in patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer, metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, and non-metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer with biochemical recurrence at high risk for metastasis (FDA.gov).

drugs.description: Imfinzi (durvalumab) is a monoclonal antibody that binds to and inhibits PD-L1 (CD274), potentially resulting in increased immune response to tumors (PMID: 25943534, PMID: 28214651). Imfinzi (durvalumab) is FDA-approved for use in patients with unresectable, stage III non-small cell lung cancer, and limited-stage small cell lung cancer, in combination with Imjudo (tremelimumab) and platinum-based chemotherapy in patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without sensitizing EGFR or ALK mutations, in combination with platinum-based chemotherapy as neoadjuvant therapy followed by surgery and adjuvant Imfinzi (durvalumab) in patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer, in combination with etoposide and carboplatin or cisplatin in patients with extensive stage small cell lung cancer, in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine in patients with locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer, in combination with Imjudo (tremelimumab) in adult patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma, and in combination with carboplatin plus paclitaxel followed by single-agent Imfinzi (durvalumab) in adult patients with mismatch repair deficient endometrial cancer (FDA.gov).

associations.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is included in guidelines as preferred second-line therapy for patients with recurrent unresectable or stage IV (M1) triple-receptor negative breast cancer harboring germline BRCA1/2 mutations, and as preferred first-line therapy for those with CD274 (PD-L1) expression level of CPS < 10 (category 1) (NCCN.org). (Approval status: Guideline)

drugs.name: Talazoparib
drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). Talzenna (talazoparib) is FDA approved for use in patients with ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, and in combination with Xtandi (enzalutamide) in patients with homologous recombination repair gene (ATM, ATR, BRCA1/2, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, MLH1, MRE11A, NBN, PALB2, or RAD51C)-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (FDA.gov).

variantDescription: BRCA2 mutant indicates an unspecified mutation in the BRCA2 gene.

gene.description: BRCA2, breast cancer type 2 susceptibility protein, is a tumor suppressor involved in the homologous recombination pathway for double-strand DNA repair, thereby playing a role in genome stability (PMID: 27530658). BRCA2 germline mutations increase the risk of developing ovarian and/or breast cancer (PMID: 23364291) and somatic mutations are highest in colon, NSCLC, and ovarian cancers (PMID: 27283171).

associations.description: Germline BRCA1/2 mutations are associated with increased risk of developing prostate cancer (NCCN.org). (Approval status: Guideline)

drugs.name: ABT-767

(Approval status: Phase II)

associations.description: In a Phase I clinical trial, the combination of Veliparib (ABT-888) and Paraplatin (carboplatin) demonstrated preliminary efficacy in metastatic breast cancer patients, with partial response in 25% (4/16) and stable disease in 62.5% (10/16) of patients with BRCA1/2 mutations or Fanconi Anemia pathway defects (J Clin Oncol 32:5s, 2014 (suppl; abstr 1074)). drugs.name: Carboplatin
drugs.description: Paraplatin (carboplatin) is a second-generation platinum compound and is activated intracellularly to form reactive platinum complexes that cross link DNA with DNA and with proteins. This induces apoptosis and inhibits cell growth (NCI Drug Dictionary).

drugs.name: Veliparib
drugs.description: Veliparib (ABT-888) is a PARP1 and PARP2 inhibitor, which inhibits DNA repair and induces lethality in homologous recombination deficient cells, and may enhance the sensitivity of chemotherapeutic agents (PMID: 26251615, PMID: 31074636, PMID: 32452601).

associations.description: In a Phase II clinical trial, Veliparib (ABT-888) demonstrated preliminary clinical activity in patients with BRCA2-mutant metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer, with an overall response rate of 66% (2/3) and clinical benefit rate of 100% (3/3) (J Clin Oncol 33, 2015 (suppl 7; abstr 170)). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Bevacizumab

drugs.name: Paclitaxel

associations.description: In a Phase I trial, Talzenna (talazoparib) treatment resulted in an objective response rate of 41.7% (5/12, 1 complete response, 4 partial responses), a clinical benefit rate of 66.7%, and a median progression-free survival of 36.4 weeks in ovarian cancer patients harboring germline deleterious BRCA1/2 mutations (PMID: 28242752; NCT01286987). (Approval status: Phase I)

drugs.name: Talazoparib
drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). associations.description: In a retrospective analysis of two Phase II trials (ARIEL 2 and Study 10), Rubraca (rucaparib) treatment resulted in an objective response rate of 54% (21/39) in patients with epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring deleterious germline or somatic BRCA1/2 mutations who had received 2 or more chemotherapies (PMID: 28751443; NCT01891344, NCT01482715). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Rucaparib
drugs.description: Rubraca (rucaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in accumulation of DNA damage and chemosensitization of tumor cells (PMID: 17363489). Rubraca (rucaparib) is FDA approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation, and for treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation (germline and/or somatic) who received anti-androgen therapy and a taxane-based therapy (FDA.gov).

associations.description: Paraplatin (carboplatin) is included in guidelines as preferred first-line therapy for patients with recurrent unresectable or stage IV (M1) triple-receptor negative breast cancer harboring germline BRCA1/2 mutations and with CD274 (PD-L1) expression level of CPS < 10 (category 1) (NCCN.org). (Approval status: Guideline)

drugs.name: Carboplatin
drugs.description: Paraplatin (carboplatin) is a second-generation platinum compound and is activated intracellularly to form reactive platinum complexes that cross link DNA with DNA and with proteins. This induces apoptosis and inhibits cell growth (NCI Drug Dictionary).

(Approval status: Guideline)

associations.description: In a Phase II trial, the addition of Veliparib (ABT-888) to Gemzar (gemcitabine) and Platinol (cisplatin) in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients with either a germline BRCA1, BRCA2, or PALB2 inactivating mutation did not improve response rate (RR) compared to Gemzar (gemcitabine) and Platinol (cisplatin) alone, with 74.1% (20/27) vs 65.2% (15/23), P=0.55, and led to similar median progression-free survival, 10.1 vs 9.7 mo, P=0.73, and median overall survival, 15.5 vs 16.4 mo, P=0.6 (PMID: 31976786). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Gemcitabine

drugs.name: Veliparib
drugs.description: Veliparib (ABT-888) is a PARP1 and PARP2 inhibitor, which inhibits DNA repair and induces lethality in homologous recombination deficient cells, and may enhance the sensitivity of chemotherapeutic agents (PMID: 26251615, PMID: 31074636, PMID: 32452601).

drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). associations.description: In a Phase II trial, patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma harboring either a germline BRCA1, BRCA2, or PALB2 inactivating mutation demonstrated a response rate of 65.2% (15/23), a median progression-free survival of 9.7 months, a median overall survival of 16.4 months, and a disease control rate of 78.3% (18/23) when treated with a combination of Gemzar (gemcitabine) and Platinol (cisplatin) (PMID: 31976786). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Gemcitabine
drugs.description: Gemzar (gemcitabine) is converted in cells to difluorodeoxycytidine di- and triphosphate (dFdCDP, dFdCTP), which act to inhibit ribonucleoside reductase and as a deoxynucleotide analog respectively, resulting in DNA strand termination and apoptosis (NCI Drug Dictionary).

drugs.name: Cisplatin
drugs.description: Platinol (cisplatin) is a platinum based chemotherapeutic, which is FDA approved for bladder, ovarian, and testicular cancers (NCI Drug Dictionary).

associations.description: In a Phase I/II trial (TRESR), RP-3500 treatment led to a response rate of 12% (13/113), clinical benefit rate (CBR) of 42% (47/113), and median progression-free survival (mPFS) of 15 weeks in advanced solid tumor patients with inactivating mutations in DNA repair genes in Phase I, including BRCA2 with a CBR of 35.7% (5/14), and with a CBR of 75% and mPFS of 35 weeks in 20 ovarian cancer patients (PMID: 37277454; NCT04497116). (Approval status: Phase I)

drugs.name: RP-3500
drugs.description: RP-3500 binds to and inhibits ATR, which may lead to decreased downstream signaling and inhibition of tumor growth (PMID: 34911817).

drugs.name: Saruparib

associations.description: In a Phase II trial (TAPUR), Lynparza (olaparib) treatment in patients with advanced solid tumors harboring a mutation in BRCA1 or BRCA2 led to an objective response rate of 25% (8/32, 2 complete responses (CR) and 6 partial responses (PR), with 1 CR and 4 PRs in patients with BRCA2 mutations), a disease control rate of 41% (13/32), a median progression-free survival of 15.7 weeks, and an overall survival of 45 weeks (Ann Oncol (2022) 33 (suppl_7): S583-S584; NCT02693535). (Approval status: Phase II)

associations.description: In a Phase III trial (ARIEL4), Rubraca (rucaparib) treatment resulted in an improved median progression-free survival (7.4 months vs 5.7 months, p=0.0010) and similar objective response rate (40% vs 32%) compared to standard-of-care chemotherapy in patients with relapsed ovarian, fallopian tube, or peritoneal cancer harboring deleterious germline or somatic BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations (PMID: 35298906; NCT02855944). (Approval status: Phase III)

drugs.name: Rucaparib
drugs.description: Rubraca (rucaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in accumulation of DNA damage and chemosensitization of tumor cells (PMID: 17363489). Rubraca (rucaparib) is FDA approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation, and for treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation (germline and/or somatic) who received anti-androgen therapy and a taxane-based therapy (FDA.gov).

references.title: Rucaparib versus standard-of-care chemotherapy in patients with relapsed ovarian cancer and a deleterious BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation (ARIEL4): an international, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial.

associations.description: In a Phase II trial (BAYOU), Lynparza (olaparib) and Imfinzi (durvalumab) improved median progression-free survival (5.6 vs 1.8 mo, HR 0.18) compared to Imfinzi (durvalumab) and placebo in a subgroup of patients with metastatic urothelial carcinoma harboring inactivating mutations in DNA damage repair genes (n=17), with 4.6% of the tumors harboring BRCA2 inactivating mutations (PMID: 35737919; NCT03459846). (Approval status: Case Reports/Case Series)

drugs.name: Durvalumab
drugs.description: Imfinzi (durvalumab) is a monoclonal antibody that binds to and inhibits PD-L1 (CD274), potentially resulting in increased immune response to tumors (PMID: 25943534, PMID: 28214651). Imfinzi (durvalumab) is FDA-approved for use in patients with unresectable, stage III non-small cell lung cancer, and limited-stage small cell lung cancer, in combination with Imjudo (tremelimumab) and platinum-based chemotherapy in patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without sensitizing EGFR or ALK mutations, in combination with platinum-based chemotherapy as neoadjuvant therapy followed by surgery and adjuvant Imfinzi (durvalumab) in patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer, in combination with etoposide and carboplatin or cisplatin in patients with extensive stage small cell lung cancer, in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine in patients with locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer, in combination with Imjudo (tremelimumab) in adult patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma, and in combination with carboplatin plus paclitaxel followed by single-agent Imfinzi (durvalumab) in adult patients with mismatch repair deficient endometrial cancer (FDA.gov).

associations.description: In a Phase II trial (JAVELIN), Talzenna (talazoparib) plus Bavencio (avelumab) did not meet prespecified futility requirements with an objective response rate (ORR) of 26.4% (42/159, 9 complete and 33 partial responses) in advanced solid tumor patients harboring BRCA1/2 inactivating mutations, and ORR was 32.0% (39/122) in BRCA-dependent (breast, ovarian, prostate, pancreatic cancer, uterine leiomyosarcoma) and 8.1% (3/37) in non-BRCA-dependent tumor types (PMID: 36394867; NCT03565991). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Talazoparib
drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). Talzenna (talazoparib) is FDA approved for use in patients with ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, and in combination with Xtandi (enzalutamide) in patients with homologous recombination repair gene (ATM, ATR, BRCA1/2, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, MLH1, MRE11A, NBN, PALB2, or RAD51C)-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (FDA.gov).

drugs.name: Avelumab
drugs.description: Bavencio (avelumab) is a monoclonal antibody binds to human immunosuppressive ligand programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1, CD274) and blocks protein signaling, resulting in immune regulation and antitumor immunity (PMID: 26014098). Bavencio (avelumab) is FDA-approved for use in adult and pediatric patients of 12 years or older with metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma, as maintenance therapy in locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (UC), in locally advanced or metastatic UC that progressed following chemotherapy, and in combination with axitinib as first-line therapy in advanced renal cell carcinoma (FDA.gov).

references.title: Avelumab Plus Talazoparib in Patients With BRCA1/2- or ATM-Altered Advanced Solid Tumors: Results From JAVELIN BRCA/ATM, an Open-Label, Multicenter, Phase 2b, Tumor-Agnostic Trial.

drugs.name: Niraparib

associations.description: In a Phase I trial, Talzenna (talazoparib) treatment resulted in an objective response rate of 50% (7/14, 1 complete response, 6 partial responses), a clinical benefit rate of 85.7%, and a median progression-free survival of 34.6 weeks in breast cancer patients harboring germline deleterious BRCA1/2 mutations (PMID: 28242752; NCT01286987). (Approval status: Phase I)

drugs.name: Talazoparib
drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). Talzenna (talazoparib) is FDA approved for use in patients with ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, and in combination with Xtandi (enzalutamide) in patients with homologous recombination repair gene (ATM, ATR, BRCA1/2, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, MLH1, MRE11A, NBN, PALB2, or RAD51C)-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (FDA.gov).

references.title: Phase I, Dose-Escalation, Two-Part Trial of the PARP Inhibitor Talazoparib in Patients with Advanced Germline BRCA1/2 Mutations and Selected Sporadic Cancers.

associations.description: In a Phase I trial, Talzenna (talazoparib) treatment resulted in a clinical benefit rate (CBR) of 56% (5/9) and a median progression-free survival (mPFS) of 20.4 weeks in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients harboring germline deleterious BRCA1/2 mutations, compared to a CBR of 89% (8/9) and a mPFS of 38.3 weeks in patients with non-TNBC (PMID: 28242752; NCT01286987). (Approval status: Case Reports/Case Series)

Tecentriq (atezolizumab) is FDA approved for use in PD-L1 positive (IC >/= 5%) advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma not eligible for cisplatin-containing chemotherapy, in advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma not eligible for chemotherapy, in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) progressed on platinum-containing therapy, as first-line therapy in metastatic NSCLC with high PD-L1 expression (TC>/=50% or IC>/=10%) and without EGFR or ALK alterations, for adjuvant treatment in patients with PD-L1-positive (>=1% tumor cell expression) NSCLC, in combination with bevacizumab, paclitaxel, and carboplatin as first-line therapy for non-squamous NSCLC with no EGFR or ALK aberrations, in combination with paclitaxel protein-bound and carboplatin in metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with no EGFR or ALK aberrations, in combination with carboplatin and etoposide in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer, in combination with bevacizumab in hepatocellular carcinoma without prior systemic therapy, in combination with Cotellic (cobimetinib) and Zelboraf (vemurafenib) in unresectable or metastatic BRAF V600-mutated melanoma, and in pediatric and adult patients with unresectable or metastatic alveolar soft part sarcoma (FDA.gov).

associations.description: In a Phase III (PAOLA-1) trial, the addition of Lynparza (olaparib) to first-line maintenance therapy with Avastin (bevacizumab) resulted in an improved 5-year overall survival (OS) rate (65.5 vs 48.4%) compared to placebo in patients with homologous-recombination deficient (HRD)-positive advanced ovarian cancer, with 5-year OS rate of 73.2 vs 53.8% in the subgroup with a deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA1/2 mutation (PMID: 37211045; NCT02477644). (Approval status: Phase III)

drugs.name: Talazoparib
drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). drugs.name: Enzalutamide
drugs.description: Xtandi (enzalutamide) is a second-generation small molecule inhibitor of androgen receptor, thereby resulting in decreased tumor growth (PMID: 24009414, PMID: 25945058). Xtandi (enzalutamide) is FDA-approved for use in patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer, metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, and non-metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer with biochemical recurrence at high risk for metastasis (FDA.gov).

associations.description: In a combined analysis of 6 clinical trials, PARP inhibitor therapy improved radiographic progression-free survival (NA vs 10 mo, HR 0.31) and overall survival (33 vs 24 mo, HR 0.66) compared to placebo when combined with AR pathway inhibitors in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring BRCA2 mutations, and resulted in an objective response rate of 47% (51/108) as monotherapy (PMID: 38484203; NCT02987543, NCT03732820, NCT03395197, NCT03748641, NCT02952534, NCT03148795). (Approval status: Clinical Study - Meta-analysis)

associations.description: In a Phase I trial, HRS-1167 treatment was well tolerated and resulted in an objective response rate of 41.7% (10/24, all partial responses) in patients with advanced solid tumors harboring germline or somatic BRCA1/2, PALB2, or RAD51C/D mutations, responses occurred in patients with ovarian (n=8), prostate (n=1), and pancreatic (n=1) cancer (J Clin Oncol 42, 2024 (suppl 16; abstr 3154); NCT05473624). (Approval status: Phase I)

drugs.name: HRS-1167
drugs.description: HRS-1167 inhibits PARP1, which potentially reduces tumor growth (J Clin Oncol 42, 2024 (suppl 16; abstr 3154)).

associations.description: In a preclinical study, the combination of XRD-0394 and Zejula (niraparib) synergistically inhibited viability of a pancreatic cancer cell line harboring a BRCA2 mutation in culture (PMID: 38588408). (Approval status: Preclinical - Cell culture)

drugs.name: Niraparib
drugs.description: Zejula (niraparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in the accumulation of DNA damage and apoptosis of tumor cells (PMID: 23810788). Zejula (niraparib) is FDA-approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer in complete or partial response to first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, and as maintenance therapy in patients with advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations and in complete or partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy (FDA.gov).

drugs.name: XRD-0394
drugs.description: XRD-0394 inhibits ATM and DNA-PK, potentially resulting in impaired DNA damage repair and inhibition of tumor growth (PMID: 38588408).

associations.description: In a Phase II trial, Talzenna (talazoparib) treatment resulted in a clinical benefit rate (CBR) of 22.8% (18/79, 1 complete and 7 partial responses, 10 with stable disease >/=24 weeks) in patients with advanced solid tumors harboring mutations in DNA damage repair genes, with a CBR of 32.5% (6/18) in patients with deleterious somatic BRCA1/2 mutations and a CBR of 30.6% (5/16) in patients with deleterious germline BRCA1/2 mutations (excluding ovarian and breast cancer) (PMID: 39085400; NCT02286687). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Talazoparib
drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). Talzenna (talazoparib) is FDA approved for use in patients with ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, and in combination with Xtandi (enzalutamide) in patients with homologous recombination repair gene (ATM, ATR, BRCA1/2, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, MLH1, MRE11A, NBN, PALB2, or RAD51C)-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (FDA.gov).

drugs.name: RP-3500

variantDescription: BRCA2 mutant indicates an unspecified mutation in the BRCA2 gene.

gene.description: BRCA2, breast cancer type 2 susceptibility protein, is a tumor suppressor involved in the homologous recombination pathway for double-strand DNA repair, thereby playing a role in genome stability (PMID: 27530658). BRCA2 germline mutations increase the risk of developing ovarian and/or breast cancer (PMID: 23364291) and somatic mutations are highest in colon, NSCLC, and ovarian cancers (PMID: 27283171).

associations.description: Germline BRCA1/2 mutations are associated with increased risk of developing prostate cancer (NCCN.org). (Approval status: Guideline)

references.title: NCCN.org

associations.description: In a Phase I trial, ABT-767 treatment resulted in a response rate of 18% (n=14/79) in patients with high grade serous ovarian cancer, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer or with solid tumors harboring germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations, with an overall 6 month time to progression rate of 22% (Ann Oncol (2014) 25 (suppl 4): iv150). (Approval status: Phase I)

drugs.name: ABT-767
drugs.description: ABT-767 binds to and inhibits the nuclear enzymes, PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents DNA damage repair and potentially leads to apoptosis (PMID: 28247011, PMID: 29313279).

associations.description: In a Phase II trial, Rubraca (rucaparib) treatment resulted in an objective response rate of 11% (2/19) and a disease control rate of 32% (6/19) in advanced pancreatic cancer patients with a known deleterious BRCA mutation, of whom 79% harbored a BRCA2 mutation (J Clin Oncol 34, 2016 (suppl; abstr 4110)). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Rucaparib
drugs.description: Rubraca (rucaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in accumulation of DNA damage and chemosensitization of tumor cells (PMID: 17363489). Rubraca (rucaparib) is FDA approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation, and for treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation (germline and/or somatic) who received anti-androgen therapy and a taxane-based therapy (FDA.gov).

associations.description: In a Phase I clinical trial, the combination of Veliparib (ABT-888) and Paraplatin (carboplatin) demonstrated preliminary efficacy in metastatic breast cancer patients, with partial response in 25% (4/16) and stable disease in 62.5% (10/16) of patients with BRCA1/2 mutations or Fanconi Anemia pathway defects (J Clin Oncol 32:5s, 2014 (suppl; abstr 1074)). (Approval status: Phase I)

drugs.name: Carboplatin
drugs.description: Paraplatin (carboplatin) is a second-generation platinum compound and is activated intracellularly to form reactive platinum complexes that cross link DNA with DNA and with proteins. This induces apoptosis and inhibits cell growth (NCI Drug Dictionary).

drugs.name: Veliparib
drugs.description: Veliparib (ABT-888) is a PARP1 and PARP2 inhibitor, which inhibits DNA repair and induces lethality in homologous recombination deficient cells, and may enhance the sensitivity of chemotherapeutic agents (PMID: 26251615, PMID: 31074636, PMID: 32452601).

associations.description: In a Phase II clinical trial, Veliparib (ABT-888) demonstrated preliminary clinical activity in patients with BRCA2-mutant metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer, with an overall response rate of 66% (2/3) and clinical benefit rate of 100% (3/3) (J Clin Oncol 33, 2015 (suppl 7; abstr 170)). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Veliparib
drugs.description: Veliparib (ABT-888) is a PARP1 and PARP2 inhibitor, which inhibits DNA repair and induces lethality in homologous recombination deficient cells, and may enhance the sensitivity of chemotherapeutic agents (PMID: 26251615, PMID: 31074636, PMID: 32452601).

associations.description: In a Phase I trial, Veliparib (ABT-888) in combination with Platinol (cisplatin) and Navelbine (vinorelbine) resulted in a greater complete response (7%, 1/14), partial response (50%, 7/14), and 6-month progression free survival rate (71%, 10/14) in Erbb2 (Her2) negative breast cancer patients harboring germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations compared to BRCA wild-type patients (PMID: 26801247). (Approval status: Phase I)

drugs.name: Talazoparib

drugs.name: Pamiparib

associations.description: In a Phase I trial, CX-5461 treatment resulted in partial response in a patient with advanced solid tumor harboring BRCA2 mutations, and stable disease in 5 additional patients, 4 of whom harboring BRCA1/2 mutations, and 1 with Li-Fraumeni syndrome (Annals of Oncology, Volume 29, Issue suppl_3, 1 March 2018, abstract 440; NCT02719977). drugs.name: CX-5461
drugs.description: CX-5461 is an RNA polymerase I (Pol I) inhibitor that inhibits rRNA synthesis, resulting in growth arrest and apoptosis in cancer cells (PMID: 26472108, PMID: 32719798).

drugs.name: Bevacizumab
drugs.description: Avastin (bevacizumab) is a monoclonal antibody that binds VEGF and inhibits binding to VEGFR, potentially resulting in decreased tumor growth (PMID: 15136787). drugs.name: Carboplatin
drugs.description: Paraplatin (carboplatin) is a second-generation platinum compound and is activated intracellularly to form reactive platinum complexes that cross link DNA with DNA and with proteins. This induces apoptosis and inhibits cell growth (NCI Drug Dictionary).

drugs.name: Paclitaxel
drugs.description: Taxol (paclitaxel) binds to tubulin to inhibit microtubule disassembly, which results in decreased cell division, and also binds to the anti-apoptotic factor Bcl-2, promoting apoptosis (NCI Drug Dictionary).

associations.description: In a Phase I trial, Truqap (capivasertib) and Lynparza (olaparib) combination therapy was well-tolerated and resulted in a clinical benefit (CB) rate of 44.6% (25/56) in patients with advanced solid tumors, 66.7% (2/3) of the prostate cancer patients harboring germline BRCA1/2 mutations achieved CB (PMID: 32532747; NCT02338622). (Approval status: Case Reports/Case Series)

drugs.name: Capivasertib
drugs.description: Truqap (capivasertib) decreases PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling by inhibition of AKT1, AKT2, and AKT3, potentially resulting in decreased cell proliferation (PMID: 22294718, PMID: 32532747, PMID: 32312891). Truqap (capivasertib) in combination with Faslodex (fulvestrant) is FDA-approved for use in patients with hormone receptor-positive, ERBB2 (HER2)-negative, locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with one or more PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-alterations (FDA.gov).

Lynparza (olaparib) is FDA approved for treatment of ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, ovarian cancer with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations and received 3 or more prior therapies, metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations as a maintenance therapy, metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline or somatic homologous recombination repair gene mutations who progressed following enzalutamide or abiraterone, in combination with abiraterone in patients with mCRPC harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA mutations, as a maintenance therapy in recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer and in epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline or somatic BRCA mutation, and in combination with Avastin (bevacizumab) as maintenance therapy in HDR defective epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer as defined by deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA mutation, and/or genomic instability (FDA.gov).

associations.description: In a Phase I trial, Veliparib (ABT-888) and Paraplatin (carboplatin) combination therapy demonstrated acceptable toxicity, resulted in a partial response (PR) in 18.6% (8/43) and stable disease (SD) in 48.8% (21/43) of patients with advanced triple-negative breast cancer (n=39) or hormone receptor positive, Erbb2 (Her2)-negative breast cancer (n=5), 28.6% (2/7) and 71.4% (5/7) of patients harboring BRCA1/2 mutations achieved PR and SD, respectively (PMID: 32452601;NCT01251874). (Approval status: Phase I)

drugs.name: Carboplatin
drugs.description: Paraplatin (carboplatin) is a second-generation platinum compound and is activated intracellularly to form reactive platinum complexes that cross link DNA with DNA and with proteins. This induces apoptosis and inhibits cell growth (NCI Drug Dictionary).

drugs.name: Veliparib
drugs.description: Veliparib (ABT-888) is a PARP1 and PARP2 inhibitor, which inhibits DNA repair and induces lethality in homologous recombination deficient cells, and may enhance the sensitivity of chemotherapeutic agents (PMID: 26251615, PMID: 31074636, PMID: 32452601).

associations.description: In a Phase II trial (NEOTALA), neoadjuvant Talzenna (talazoparib) treatment was well tolerated and resulted in a pathologic complete response (pCR) of 45.8% (22/48) and a residual cancer burden (RCB) 0/I rate of 45.8% (22/48) in the evaluable population and a pCR of 49.2% (30/61) and RCB 0/I rate of 50.8% (31/61) in the intent to treat population of patients with triple-negative breast cancer harboring germline mutations in BRCA1 or BRCA2 (PMID: 37318349; NCT03499353). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Talazoparib
drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). Talzenna (talazoparib) is FDA approved for use in patients with ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, and in combination with Xtandi (enzalutamide) in patients with homologous recombination repair gene (ATM, ATR, BRCA1/2, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, MLH1, MRE11A, NBN, PALB2, or RAD51C)-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (FDA.gov).

drugs.name: Rucaparib
drugs.description: Rubraca (rucaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in accumulation of DNA damage and chemosensitization of tumor cells (PMID: 17363489). Rubraca (rucaparib) is FDA approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation, and for treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation (germline and/or somatic) who received anti-androgen therapy and a taxane-based therapy (FDA.gov).

associations.description: In a Phase III trial (OlympiAD) that supported FDA approval, Lynparza (olaparib) treatment resulted in significantly improved median progression-free survival (7.0 vs 4.2 mo, HR=0.58, p<0.001) and higher response rate (59.9% vs 28.8%) compared to standard chemotherapy in ERBB2 (HER2)-negative metastatic breast cancer patients harboring a deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutation who had 2 or less prior chemotherapy (PMID: 28578601; NCT02000622). (Approval status: FDA approved - On Companion Diagnostic)

drugs.name: Olaparib
drugs.description: Lynparza (olaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, resulting in inhibition of DNA repair and lethality in homologous-recombination deficient cells, and may be a sensitizing agent for chemotherapy and radiotherapy (PMID: 25028150, PMID: 24225019). associations.description: In a Phase I trial, Talzenna (talazoparib) treatment resulted in an objective response rate of 41.7% (5/12, 1 complete response, 4 partial responses), a clinical benefit rate of 66.7%, and a median progression-free survival of 36.4 weeks in ovarian cancer patients harboring germline deleterious BRCA1/2 mutations (PMID: 28242752; NCT01286987). (Approval status: Phase I)

drugs.name: Talazoparib
drugs.description: Talzenna (talazoparib) is an inhibitor of PARP1 and PARP2, which prevents the DNA repair of single strand DNA breaks, thus causing the accumulation of DNA strand breaks, genomic instability and apoptosis, and leads to lethality in homologous recombination repair deficient cells (PMID: 28242752). Talzenna (talazoparib) is FDA approved for use in patients with ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, and in combination with Xtandi (enzalutamide) in patients with homologous recombination repair gene (ATM, ATR, BRCA1/2, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, MLH1, MRE11A, NBN, PALB2, or RAD51C)-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (FDA.gov).

references.title: Phase I, Dose-Escalation, Two-Part Trial of the PARP Inhibitor Talazoparib in Patients with Advanced Germline BRCA1/2 Mutations and Selected Sporadic Cancers.

associations.description: In a retrospective analysis of two Phase II trials (ARIEL 2 and Study 10), Rubraca (rucaparib) treatment resulted in an objective response rate of 54% (21/39) in patients with epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring deleterious germline or somatic BRCA1/2 mutations who had received 2 or more chemotherapies (PMID: 28751443; NCT01891344, NCT01482715). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Rucaparib
drugs.description: Rubraca (rucaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in accumulation of DNA damage and chemosensitization of tumor cells (PMID: 17363489). Rubraca (rucaparib) is FDA approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation, and for treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation (germline and/or somatic) who received anti-androgen therapy and a taxane-based therapy (FDA.gov).

(Approval status: Guideline)

drugs.name: Carboplatin
drugs.description: Paraplatin (carboplatin) is a second-generation platinum compound and is activated intracellularly to form reactive platinum complexes that cross link DNA with DNA and with proteins. This induces apoptosis and inhibits cell growth (NCI Drug Dictionary).

(Approval status: Guideline)

associations.description: In a Phase II trial, the addition of Veliparib (ABT-888) to Gemzar (gemcitabine) and Platinol (cisplatin) in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients with either a germline BRCA1, BRCA2, or PALB2 inactivating mutation did not improve response rate (RR) compared to Gemzar (gemcitabine) and Platinol (cisplatin) alone, with 74.1% (20/27) vs 65.2% (15/23), P=0.55, and led to similar median progression-free survival, 10.1 vs 9.7 mo, P=0.73, and median overall survival, 15.5 vs 16.4 mo, P=0.6 (PMID: 31976786). (Approval status: Phase II)

associations.description: In a Phase II trial (TOPARP-B), Lynparza (olaparib) treatment resulted in a composite overall response rate of 83.3% (25/30) and a RECIST objective response rate of 52.4% (11/21) in patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring deleterious mutations or homozygous deletion of BRCA1/2 (PMID: 31806540; NCT01682772). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Olaparib
drugs.description: Lynparza (olaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, resulting in inhibition of DNA repair and lethality in homologous-recombination deficient cells, and may be a sensitizing agent for chemotherapy and radiotherapy (PMID: 25028150, PMID: 24225019). Lynparza (olaparib) is FDA approved for treatment of ERBB2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations, ovarian cancer with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations and received 3 or more prior therapies, metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations as a maintenance therapy, metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline or somatic homologous recombination repair gene mutations who progressed following enzalutamide or abiraterone, in combination with abiraterone in patients with mCRPC harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA mutations, as a maintenance therapy in recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer and in epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline or somatic BRCA mutation, and in combination with Avastin (bevacizumab) as maintenance therapy in HDR defective epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer as defined by deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA mutation, and/or genomic instability (FDA.gov).

associations.description: In a Phase II trial (QUADRA), Zejula (niraparib) demonstrated efficacy in patients with ovarian, fallopian tube, and primary peritoneal cancer who have received 3 or more chemotherapies, particularly in those harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA1/2 mutations or with homologous recombination deficiency (HRD)-positive tumors, resulting in an overall response rate of 29% (18/63) and 15% (29/189), and an overall survival of 26.0 and 19.0 months, respectively (PMID: 30948273; NCT02354586). (Approval status: Phase II)

drugs.name: Niraparib
drugs.description: Zejula (niraparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in the accumulation of DNA damage and apoptosis of tumor cells (PMID: 23810788). Zejula (niraparib) is FDA-approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer in complete or partial response to first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, and as maintenance therapy in patients with advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutations and in complete or partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy (FDA.gov).

references.title: Niraparib monotherapy for late-line treatment of ovarian cancer (QUADRA): a multicentre, open-label, single-arm, phase 2 trial.

(Approval status: FDA approved - On Companion Diagnostic)

associations.description: In a Phase II trial (TRITON2) that supported FDA approval, Rubraca (rucaparib) treatment resulted in an objective response rate of 43.5% (27/62) and a PSA response rate of 54.8% (63/115) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who progressed on 1 or more anti-androgen and 1 taxane-based therapy and harboring deleterious BRCA1/2 germline or somatic mutations as detected by approved assays, including nonsense, frameshift, rearrangement, splice site variants (PMID: 32795228; NCT02952534). (Approval status: FDA approved - On Companion Diagnostic)

drugs.name: Rucaparib
drugs.description: Rubraca (rucaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in accumulation of DNA damage and chemosensitization of tumor cells (PMID: 17363489). Rubraca (rucaparib) is FDA approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation, and for treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation (germline and/or somatic) who received anti-androgen therapy and a taxane-based therapy (FDA.gov).

associations.description: In a Phase III (PAOLA-1) trial that supported FDA approval, addition of maintenance Lynparza (olaparib) to Avastin (bevacizumab) following standard first-line therapy improved median progression-free survival compared to placebo (37.2 vs 17.7 mo, HR=0.33) in patients with advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneum cancer who were homologous-recombination deficient, as defined by deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA mutations or genomic instability (PMID: 31851799; NCT02477644). (Approval status: FDA approved - On Companion Diagnostic)

drugs.name: Bevacizumab
drugs.description: Avastin (bevacizumab) is a monoclonal antibody that binds VEGF and inhibits binding to VEGFR, potentially resulting in decreased tumor growth (PMID: 15136787). associations.description: In a Phase III trial (ARIEL4), Rubraca (rucaparib) treatment resulted in an improved median progression-free survival (7.4 months vs 5.7 months, p=0.0010) and similar objective response rate (40% vs 32%) compared to standard-of-care chemotherapy in patients with relapsed ovarian, fallopian tube, or peritoneal cancer harboring deleterious germline or somatic BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations (PMID: 35298906; NCT02855944). (Approval status: Phase III)

drugs.name: Rucaparib
drugs.description: Rubraca (rucaparib) binds to and inhibits PARP, which may result in accumulation of DNA damage and chemosensitization of tumor cells (PMID: 17363489). Rubraca (rucaparib) is FDA approved for use as maintenance therapy in patients with platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation, and for treatment in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer harboring a deleterious BRCA mutation (germline and/or somatic) who received anti-androgen therapy and a taxane-based therapy (FDA.gov).

(Approval status: Case Reports/Case Series)
